1	function Test-MtMobileThreatDefenseConnectors {
2	    <#
3	    .SYNOPSIS
4	    Check the Intune Mobile Threat Defense Connectors.
5	    .DESCRIPTION
6	    This command checks the Mobile Threat Defense Connectors configured in Microsoft Intune to determine their status and connectivity.
7	
8	    .EXAMPLE
9	    Test-MtMobileThreatDefenseConnectors
10	
11	    Returns true if all Mobile Threat Defense Connectors are enabled and have recent heartbeats, false otherwise.
12	
13	    .LINK
14	    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtMobileThreatDefenseConnectors
15	    #>
16	    [MaesterTest(
17	        Id = 'MT.1098',
18	        Title = 'Mobile Threat Defense Connectors should be healthy',
19	        Product = 'intune',
20	        RelatedProduct = 'defender',
21	        Feature = 'tenant-administration',
22	        Area = 'devices',
23	        ResourceType = 'Connector',
24	        Severity = 'High',
25	        UserImpact = 'Low',
26	        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
27	        Mitre = 'None',
28	        Service = 'Graph',
29	        License = 'INTUNE_A',
30	        Author = 'nicolonsky',
31	        Contributor = ('Mynster9361', 'FiraSenax')
32	    )]
33	    [CmdletBinding()]
34	    [OutputType([bool])]
35	    [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSUseSingularNouns', '', Justification = 'Multiple MTD connectors can exist.')]
36	    param()
37	
38	    # MTD Connector IDs and Names
39	    # Source: https://github.com/microsoft/Microsoft365DSC/blob/Dev/Modules/Microsoft365DSC/DSCResources/REDACTED.psm1
40	    $mtdConnectorInformation = @{
41	        '2c7790de-8b02-4814-85cf-e0c59380dee8' = 'Lookout for Work'
42	        '28fd67fd-b179-4629-a8b0-dad420b697c7' = 'Symantec Endpoint Protection'
43	        'd3ddeae8-441f-4681-b80f-aef644f7195a' = 'Check Point Harmony Mobile'
44	        '08a8455c-48dd-45ff-ad82-7211355354f3' = 'Zimperium'
45	        '8d0ed095-8191-4bd3-8a41-953b22d51ff7' = 'Pradeo'
46	        '860d3ab4-8fd1-45f5-89cd-ecf51e4f92e5' = 'BETTER Mobile Security'
47	        '870b252b-0ef0-4707-8847-50fc571472b3' = 'Sophos'
48	        '1f58d6d2-02cc-4c80-b008-1bfe7396a10a' = 'Jamf Trust'
49	        '4873197-ffec-4dfc-9816-db65f34c7cb9'  = 'Trellix Mobile Security'
50	        'a447eca6-a986-4d3f-9838-5862bf50776c' = 'CylancePROTECT Mobile'
51	        '4928f0f6-2660-4f69-b4c5-5170ec921f7b' = 'Trend Micro'
52	        'bb13fe25-ce1f-45aa-b278-cabbc6b9072e' = 'SentinelOne'
53	        'c2b688fe-48c0-464b-a89c-67041aa8fcb2' = 'Windows Security Center'
54	        '29ee2d98-e795-475f-a0f8-0802dc3384a9' = 'CrowdStrike Falcon for Mobile'
55	        'fc780465-2017-40d4-a0c5-307022471b92' = 'Microsoft Defender for Endpoint'
56	        'fc06ff9b-e2f9-4221-9a68-465684ee8662' = 'iVerify'
57	    }
58	
59	    try {
60	        Write-Verbose 'Retrieving Mobile Threat Defense Connectors status...'
61	        $mobileThreatDefenseConnectors = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'deviceManagement/mobileThreatDefenseConnectors' -ApiVersion beta
62	
63	        if (($mobileThreatDefenseConnectors | Measure-Object).Count -eq 0) {
64	            throw [System.Management.Automation.ItemNotFoundException]::new('No Mobile Threat Defense Connectors found.')
65	        }
66	
67	        $testResultMarkdown = "Mobile Threat Defense Connector Status:`n"
68	        $testResultMarkdown += "| Name | LastHeartbeatDateTime | PartnerState | Reason |`n"
69	        $testResultMarkdown += "| --- | --- | --- | --- |`n"
70	
71	        $connectorStatus = foreach ($connector in $mobileThreatDefenseConnectors) {
72	
73	            if ($mtdConnectorInformation.ContainsKey($connector.id)) {
74	                Write-Verbose ('Found {0} Connector.' -f $mtdConnectorInformation[$connector.id])
75	                $connectorName = $mtdConnectorInformation[$connector.id]
76	            } else {
77	                Write-Verbose ('Found Unknown Third Party Mobile Threat Defense Connector: {0}' -f $connector.id)
78	                $connectorName = $connector.id
79	            }
80	
81	            $isConnected = $connector.partnerState -eq 'enabled'
82	            $reasons = @(switch ($connector.partnerState) {
83	                'enabled' { break }
84	                'notSetUp' { 'Setup is incomplete; device threat messages are blocked. Complete setup in Intune and with the partner, or remove an unused connector.' }
85	                'unavailable' { 'The connector is deprovisioned; device threat messages are blocked. Ask the MTD partner to provision it again.' }
86	                'available' { 'Setup is complete. Turn on a platform toggle to enable the connector.' }
87	                'unresponsive' { 'The connector is unresponsive. After its configured unresponsiveness threshold, Intune ignores its compliance state. Check the partner service and connectivity.' }
88	                'error' { 'The connector reported an error. Check the partner service for the error details.' }
89	                default { 'Unrecognized connector state. Review the connector in Intune and with the partner.' }
90	            })
91	
92	            $heartbeat = if ($connector.lastHeartbeatDateTime) { [datetime]$connector.lastHeartbeatDateTime } else { [datetime]::MinValue }
93	            if ($heartbeat.Year -eq 1) {
94	                $heartbeatDisplay = 'Never received'
95	                $syncIsRecent = $false
96	                $reasons += 'No heartbeat has been received. Complete setup and verify that the partner can communicate with Intune.'
97	            } else {
98	                $heartbeatDisplay = [string]$connector.lastHeartbeatDateTime
99	                # At most one completed day since the heartbeat, so less than 48 hours.
100	                $syncIsRecent = [System.Math]::Floor(((Get-Date) - $heartbeat).TotalDays) -le 1
101	                if (-not $syncIsRecent) {
102	                    $reasons += 'No heartbeat in the last 48 hours. Check the partner service and connectivity.'
103	                }
104	            }
105	
106	            if ($isConnected -and $syncIsRecent) {
107	                $reasons = @('Enabled with a recent heartbeat.')
108	            }
109	
110	            $nameMarkdown = Get-MtSafeMarkdown -Text $connectorName
111	            $heartbeatMarkdown = Get-MtSafeMarkdown -Text $heartbeatDisplay
112	            $stateMarkdown = Get-MtSafeMarkdown -Text ([string]$connector.partnerState)
113	            $testResultMarkdown += "| $nameMarkdown | $heartbeatMarkdown | $stateMarkdown | $($reasons -join ' ') |`n"
114	            Write-Output ($isConnected -and $syncIsRecent)
115	        }
116	
117	        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
118	        return $connectorStatus -notcontains $false
119	    } catch [System.Management.Automation.ItemNotFoundException] {
120	        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason $_
121	    }
122	}

content.text:
julien-ly is right about Trellix. On Windows Security Center, Maester's ID is the one confirmed by a live tenant, and Microsoft365DSC's value is the one with no tenant evidence behind it.

**Trellix (`4873197-ffec-4dfc-9816-db65f34c7cb9`): confirmed wrong.**
- The first block has seven hex characters, so it can never equal a connector ID that Graph returns.
- Microsoft365DSC's [MSFT_IntuneMobileThreatDefenseConnector.psm1](https://github.com/microsoft/Microsoft365DSC/blob/Dev/Modules/Microsoft365DSC/DscResources/MSFT_IntuneMobileThreatDefenseConnector/MSFT_IntuneMobileThreatDefenseConnector.psm1) has the same typo, and it has been in Maester since Nicola's first Intune checks.
- It only affects the name shown. The table is used only to look up a display name ([Test.MT.1098.ps1:73](tests/maester/intune/Test.MT.1098.ps1:73)), so a tenant's Trellix connector appears as its raw ID. Pass or fail doesn't change.
- I couldn't find the correct ID anywhere public. Searching the last four blocks turns up nothing. Fixing it properly needs someone with a Trellix connector to share the `id` from `deviceManagement/mobileThreatDefenseConnectors`.

**Windows Security Center: keep `c2b688fe-48c0-464b-a89c-67041aa8fcb2`.**
- Mynster9361 added it in maester365/maester#1614.
- In maester365/maester#2595 they created the connector in the portal ("Select 'Windows Security Center' → Create"). They then pasted the raw Graph response, which has that ID and `windowsMobileApplicationManagementEnabled: True`. That setting fits Windows Security Center, which is a Windows MAM connector.
- DSC's `e6f777f8-e4c2-4a5b-be01-50b5c124bc7f` doesn't appear in any tenant output I could find. I wouldn't add it unless someone shows a tenant returning it.

**One more thing in the same file:** the source comment at [Test.MT.1098.ps1:39](tests/maester/intune/Test.MT.1098.ps1:39) points at `REDACTED.psm1`. That's the wrong DSC resource, and the table has moved away from DSC anyway (Windows Security Center, iVerify).

The fix PR would:
- Remove the Trellix entry.
- Correct the source comment, noting which IDs were confirmed from tenants.

That's a short branch off `main`, separate from this website branch.

Here's a reply to julien-ly, ready to post once you approve it:

> Thanks, both worth checking.
>
> - **Trellix:** agreed. With seven characters in its first block it can never match, so a Trellix connector shows as its raw ID in the result. Pass/fail isn't affected. We'll remove the entry. If anyone has a Trellix connector, the `id` from `deviceManagement/mobileThreatDefenseConnectors` would let us add it back correctly.
> - **Windows Security Center:** we'll keep `c2b688fe-48c0-464b-a89c-67041aa8fcb2`. That's the ID Graph returned in a live tenant right after the connector was created (#2595). We haven't seen DSC's `e6f777f8-…` from a tenant. If you have one that returns it, please share it and we'll add it.

content.text:
I can use Lokka with Elapora, but the read failed, so I don't have the Trellix ID yet. I switched Lokka to Elapora (merill@elapora.com) and asked for `deviceManagement/mobileThreatDefenseConnectors`. Graph returned 403. That endpoint needs `DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All`, and Lokka's token for Elapora only has `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` and `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All`.

Lokka can add the missing permission. Adding it means granting a new delegated permission in the tenant, so I'm asking before I do it. It's read-only.

Even with the permission, Graph only lists connectors that have been created in that tenant. If Elapora has no Trellix connector, the list won't include its ID. The way to get it would be to create a Trellix connector in Intune (Tenant administration → Connectors and tokens → Mobile Threat Defense → Create → Trellix Mobile Security), read the ID, then delete the connector. That writes to the tenant, so I wouldn't do it without a separate yes from you. Creating it from the portal yourself is also quick.

Then run the command again and delete the connector afterwards.
